miniProject.title: Crash-safe segmented storage with defensible acknowledgement boundaries
miniProject.brief: Extend `loglab` with a checksummed segmented log and a crash-safe key-value projection in `storage/`. Use independent operation and persistence models to establish recovery before timing anything on your machine, then explain durability, compaction and access costs from retained histories and byte accounting.
steps: Define the storage fault model and separate buffered, flushed and durable acknowledgement paths. Build versioned segmented write-ahead records with offsets, bounded lengths and identity-bound checksums; compare scans and key-value operations against independent byte-decoding and dictionary models, retaining record fixtures and state-transition histories.

Inject crashes before and after every append, checksum write, flush, sync, index update, manifest publication and acknowledgement, including short, reordered and delayed writes, storage-full and sync errors. Compare recovery with an independent stable-byte model; retain acknowledged-prefix verdicts separating process loss from simulated OS loss.

Implement checkpoint-plus-suffix recovery and index rebuild, including crashes during replay. Check against full replay of the trusted record history; retain idempotence, lost-write and misdirected-record tests. Repair only contract-permitted incomplete tails; surface possible acknowledged loss or interior corruption terminally without inventing records.

Rebuild hash and sparse indexes, add memtable flushes into sorted runs and Bloom filters. Compare point and range results against full scans, Bloom decisions against exact membership and sizing math; retain split-invariant fixtures and separate CMU B+ Tree single-threaded test results with page-capacity reasoning.

Implement projection compaction with retained tombstones, complete synced output files and atomic manifest replacement, including directory sync. Compare recovered live state against uncompacted replay at every publication boundary; retain a planted resurrection failure, its repair and snapshot-retention tests without silently compacting away replayable log records.

Choose row-oriented storage from point, range and analytical workload byte models; contrast columnar skipping with full-scan results and distinguish file, table and catalog metadata. Check compression round trips and buffer ownership on fixed traces; retain separate CMU Buffer Pool Manager results and cache-state protocols.

Pass randomized model-based operations and planted-delete regressions, retaining shrunk failures. Then repeat sync-policy, compaction and cache-controlled sequential/random-read comparisons; keep sync/recovery times, latency distributions, throughput, resource use, read/write/space amplification and observer overhead, reconciled with byte ledgers, versions, workloads and cache-state evidence.
deliverables: The segmented WAL, key-value projection, checkpoint recovery, rebuildable indexes and crash-safe compaction, with acknowledgement and replay-retention contracts.
Independent dictionary and stable-byte models, exhaustive boundary fault fixtures, shrunk regressions, raw WAL histories and separate public-suite results.
A repeated measurement dossier with byte ledgers, cache-state evidence, durability limitations and retained policy trade-offs.

checks.name: CMU 15-445 Fall 2025 Project 2: B+ Tree
checks.note: Retain single-threaded insert, delete, iterator and tombstone-buffer results from the unit; your log indexes still need independent full-scan checks.

checks.name: CMU 15-445 Fall 2025 Project 1: Buffer Pool Manager
checks.note: Keep ARC, disk scheduler and page-guard results separately from your store's crash, cache-state and ownership tests.

rubric.pass: Own crash tests agree with the independent stable-byte model at every persistence boundary. The acknowledged-prefix contract survives permitted faults; unrepairable corruption halts with evidence rather than fabricated success.
rubric.strong: Delayed sync, failed sync and repeated recovery expose naive durability claims; a documented simulation-versus-filesystem boundary limits what process-kill evidence can establish.

rubric.pass: Own dictionary and full-scan checks match randomized operations, rebuilt indexes and sorted runs. Exact membership catches Bloom false negatives; sizing calculations and page invariants have independent fixtures.
rubric.strong: A planted delete or index defect produces a shrunk failing sequence, fails before repair and remains a deterministic regression across restart and flush.

rubric.pass: Own boundary tests recover old or new complete manifests and match uncompacted replay. A planted tombstone-resurrection defect fails; snapshot and log-retention contracts name which older versions must remain readable.
rubric.strong: Crashes combined with orphan cleanup or retained snapshots expose an unsafe reclamation; repaired tests preserve both live-state correctness and declared replay availability.

rubric.pass: Correctness gates precede repeated measurements. Independent byte ledgers reconcile amplification and skipping; reports name versions, workloads, cache preparation and observer overhead, separating logical I/O from device-traffic claims.
rubric.strong: Group-commit or compaction comparisons retain a losing regime; recovery time is explained by replayed bytes and sequential-versus-random read costs without claiming a universal winner.

miniProject.feedsInto: Segments, offsets, persistence events, checkpoint recovery and acknowledged-prefix oracles feed replication and consensus; manifests, retained-log contracts and corruption fixtures feed stream replay, backup, restore and the capstone's storage-fault evidence.
